podcast.body: Released in early summer 1985, this song was a commercial triumph, climbing to number three on the Hot 100 by August (her first pop top 10 hit since 1974's "Until You Come Back to Me") and number one on the R&B chart. Its video gave her first MTV appearance, and it was the second most acclaimed single of 1985 in the Pazz & Jop Critics Poll. The song, written by Narada Michael Walden, cleverly updated the Motown sound with a Bruce Springsteen influence, including a "pink Cadillac" lyric and a saxophone solo by Clarence Clemons. "It's difficult to overstate what a commercial triumph Freeway of Love was for Aritha Franklin."
